tpis: TAX-01 (Automation · Automation)
Rule-based Tax GL Analyzer for capital assets
Feasible
Rules supplied by Tax, tool built by Group IT. Live and proven on IT and Telecommunication this year.
TAX-02 (Automation · Automation)
Scale to the remaining tax categories in the CIT Tax Pack
Feasible
Seven to nine or more categories per country need the same analysis. Same pack, same method, same tool.
TAX-03 (Automation · Automation)
Scale to the other regions
Under review
The CIT Tax Pack is already standardised across APAC, LATAM and India, which is the foundation for regional scale-up.
TAX-04 (AI · AI · Automation)
AI summarises and categorises lines the rules cannot classify
Under review
Where the tool returns 'requires human analysis', AI summarises the item, categorises it and reviews the trend.
TAX-05 (AI · AI · Automation)
AI proposes rule-set updates for analyst approval
Under review
AI finds similar cases and proposes a new rule. Nothing changes without a person approving it.
TAX-06 (Process Improvement)
Capture rule knowledge in the rule set rather than in one person
Feasible
Storing approved cases in the rules strengthens continuity and lets others maintain them when the owner is away.
TAX-07 (AI · AI)
AI trend analysis to support finance decision-making
Can be explored in the future
Use the analysed population to surface trends that help the finance team, beyond the reclassification itself.
TAX-08 (AI · AI)
Explore Claude for the remaining analysis
Feasible
Stated as the next step: test whether it can assist with the analysis the rule-based tool does not cover.
TAX-09 (AI · AI · Automation)
Move to agentic AI once SAP interfacing and governance allow
Not feasible
Raised as the likely end state. Not feasible today because agentic AI cannot interface with SAP and governance is unresolved.
TAX-10 (AI · AI · Automation)
Interim route: extract to SharePoint, then analyse with an agent
Under review
Extract from SAP by script, land the data in SharePoint, and let an agent plug into Copilot to analyse it there.
TAX-11 (AI · AI)
Use chain prompting or an agent builder for consistent output
Feasible
Addresses the consistency problem directly: chain prompting returns the same result repeatedly against defined rules.
TAX-12 (Automation · AI · Automation)
Schedule the chain prompt so runs are unattended
Feasible
Removes the need to trigger the analysis manually each cycle.
TAX-13 (Automation · Automation)
Extend the tool to capital allowance identification
Can be explored in the future
With the fixed asset register, PO description, vendor master, asset class and cost centre available, qualifying capital allowance can be identified.
TAX-14 (Automation · Automation)
Extend to tax adjustments and exception identification
Can be explored in the future
Since all GL items are already in the tool, use it to identify penalties, fines, add-backs and other adjustments.
TAX-15 (Automation · AI · Automation)
Draft tax computation and auto-fill of tax forms
Can be explored in the future
Mirror the tax form for one pilot market and auto-fill it, taking the case end to end rather than stopping at analysis.
TAX-16 (Automation · Automation)
Notify the analyst when the reviewed file is ready
Feasible
Part of the target design: the tool notifies the user, who performs a final sanity check before release to the tax agent.
TAX-17 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Group IT builds from Tax-supplied rules
Feasible
The proven model: Tax owns the rules, Group IT builds the solution. Delivered in two to three months once funded.
TAX-18 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Secure data science support for the next phase
Under review
The team asked directly for exploration support, keeping the split of Tax-supplied rules and a technically built solution.
TAX-19 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Source fixed asset, vendor and cost centre data from R2R
Feasible
Fixed asset register, PO description, vendor master, asset class and cost centre are the inputs the extension needs.
TAX-20 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Leverage the Global Fixed Asset Dashboard already in build
Feasible
Referenced directly in session as an existing source of the asset information the tax extension would need.
TAX-21 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Run one market as a pilot to demonstrate to Group Tax
Feasible
Group Tax needs to see it working. A pilot market shows the method and the cost case in one place.
TAX-22 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Renegotiate third-party tax agent fees as work moves in house
Under review
Work returning in house reduces what the agent does. The market bears the fee under a global contract, so the saving is real.
TAX-23 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Align with the SFO model on who scales the analyzer
Under review
Tax is working concurrently with the SFO model and building in house, expecting to meet in the middle on who delivers.
TAX-24 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Resolve the global mandate on the third-party analysis split
Under review
Scaling is dependent on a global decision about how much analysis is directed to the third-party provider.
TAX-25 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Work with GPDD and regional leads on scalability
Under review
Engagement is already close. Other regions review on materiality rather than line by line, so the approach does not transfer unchanged.
TAX-26 (Cross-Tower Collaboration · AI)
Work with Global Digital on agentic AI governance and SAP interfacing
Can be explored in the future
The blocker is not the idea but the platform: agentic AI cannot interface with SAP and has no agreed governance yet.
TAX-27 (Cross-Tower Collaboration · AI)
Draw on Global Digital enablement for prompting and agent building
Feasible
Chain prompting, agent builder and scheduling techniques were offered in session as a way to reach consistent output.
TAX-28 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Share the rule-based analysis method with other process towers
Feasible
An explicit invitation from the presenter: any tower doing rule-driven data analysis can replicate the same approach.
TAX-29 (Cross-Tower Collaboration)
Track the USD 5,000 to USD 10,000 threshold decision
Under review
A management-level discussion. Raising the threshold pushes more assets into the P&L and increases the reclassification population.
